newsitem.title: JAPAN: POLL-Japan jobless rate seen falling slightly.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Japan jobless rate seen falling slightly.

text.p: Japan's unemployment rate is expected to ease slightly over the next two business years, a Reuters poll of economists showed on Thursday.

Forecasts from 29 economists produced an average jobless rate of 3.3 percent for the current business year, while 24 of the economists gave an average forecast of 3.2 percent for the 1998/99 business year.
Economists said employment conditions were improving and higher corporate profits should feed into wage gains and overtime, adding that this should lend support to consumer spending.
But they were divided between those who saw the rate moving only a fraction lower and others who saw a steady easing over the next two years.
"It's going to be difficult for the unemployment rate to change much, although this does not reflect a worsening jobs situation," said Mamoru Yamazaki, an economist at Paribas Capital Markets.

Young people quitting their jobs in search of better work and housewives encouraged by the economic recovery to enter the labour market would continue to exert upward pressure on the rate in the medium to long term, he said.

The unemployment rate rose to 3.5 percent in May from 3.3 percent in April, matching the record high hit in May and June 1996. Many analysts attributed the rise to an influx of people into the job market.
Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics predicted the rate would break below 3.0 percent and slump to 2.8 percent in 1998/99.
"Companies' desire to employ people is on the rise again," said Shuji Shirota, a Yamaichi Research economist, pointing to an increase in recruitment of graduates for next year.
He added, however, that, "Even so, a figure of 2.8 percent is not that great an improvement when compared with past recoveries."
The survey was conducted from July 7 to July 9.
